title: Working Out the Refundable Credit on an Insured Plan of Care
content:
**Patient Accounts Manual — Insured Plan of Care, refundable credit.**

**Clause 1 — the credit standing on the plan.** The credit standing on the plan of care is worked out from its ledger: every patient payment and every balance adjustment on the plan, less every patient charge and every refund already issued on the plan, never below zero, to the cent.

**Clause 2 — the payment returned.** The refund is returned against the patient's most recent payment on the plan.

**Clause 3 — the refundable credit.** The refundable credit is that credit, no larger than the payment it is returned against, rounded half up to the cent.

## Worked figures (hypothetical ledgers)

| Payments | Adjustments | Charges | Refunds already issued | Credit standing | Most recent payment | Refundable credit |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| $300.00 | $40.00 | $260.00 | $0.00 | $80.00 | $50.00 | $50.00 (capped at the payment) |
| $300.00 | $40.00 | $260.00 | $0.00 | $80.00 | $100.00 | $80.00 |
| $300.00 | $40.00 | $260.00 | $30.00 | $50.00 | $100.00 | $50.00 |
| $200.00 | $0.00 | $260.00 | $0.00 | $0.00 (never below zero) | $100.00 | $0.00 |

**How the ledger is read.** Payments and adjustments both reduce what the patient owes, so both add to the credit; charges and refunds already issued both reduce it. The comparison with the payment is a ceiling only: when the credit is smaller than that payment, the whole credit is refundable.
